entities.name: Trabecular plate-like phenotype
observations: In HR-pQCT/individual trabecula segmentation studies, defined by a high trabecular plate-to-rod ratio; overrepresented in Chinese-American versus Caucasian women.
In a 146-woman extreme-phenotype study, plate-like women were 25.7-fold more likely to be Chinese-American than rod-like women (95% CI 7.3–90.1); adjusted odds were 85.0 (95% CI 12.7–568.0).
The difference is strongest in premenopausal women; postmenopausal differences in absolute plate BV/TV are attenuated, although plate-to-rod ratio may remain higher.

entities.name: PMID:25069706
observations: Compared 146 Chinese-American and Caucasian women using HR-pQCT and individual trabecula segmentation; plate-like phenotype was defined as tibial plate-to-rod ratio in the highest quartile and rod-like phenotype as the lowest quartile.
Chinese-American enrichment was 25.7-fold unadjusted and 85.0-fold after constitutional and lifestyle adjustment.

entities.name: PMID:21351150
observations: In premenopausal Chinese-American versus white women, plate BV/TV was 95% higher at the radius and 80% higher at the tibia; plate-to-rod ratio was approximately twice as high, with statistically significant differences.

entities.name: PMID:23299863
observations: Premenopausal Chinese-American women had higher plate BV/TV, plate-to-rod ratio, and plate-plate junction density than white women; postmenopausal differences were smaller but plate-to-rod ratio remained higher.

entities.name: PMID:31437567
observations: In a cohort of 186 Chinese and 381 Caucasian women, premenopausal Chinese women had a 0.55-SD higher plate-to-rod ratio, associated with higher plate BV/TV and lower rod BV/TV; the plate advantage was attenuated after menopause.
